hero.thesis: One product, many kinds of user
hero.sentence: I'm a Senior Frontend Developer in Ho Chi Minh City, building frontends since 2018 and now on a UAV project at FPT Software. I've built public-facing pages in React/Next.js with SSR, and led a frontend team of 8 on a three-portal logistics platform in Angular and Nx Micro Frontend.

beats.title: VELA, taken apart
body: The VELA Logistics Platform has three portals: Core for internal operations, and Customer and Supplier for people outside the company. From July 2023 to March 2026, I was the Frontend Team Leader (hands-on) at Indo Trans Logistics, and I designed the Angular frontend architecture for all three.
The project team had 60 people. I led the frontend team of 8 and set the code review workflow, the coding standards and a GitFlow-based branching strategy.

beats.title: Core, one block
body: Core Portal is the internal operations side, a single Angular application. Take the whole drawing apart and it stays one block.
I reduced Core Portal's initial bundle from 12 MB to 3 MB through bundle analysis, dependency import optimization, code splitting and route-based lazy loading.

beats.title: Two platforms, a Host each
body: Customer Portal and Supplier Portal are two Micro Frontend platforms on Nx, each with one Host and multiple Remotes. This let teams deploy independently and develop in parallel.
beats.note: The number of Remote blocks in the drawing is illustrative, not the real count.

beats.title: Configured by tenant
body: All three portals are meant to be multi-tenant, with tenant-based configuration and isolation. For Customer and Supplier, I designed the frontend for 3 tenants.

beats.title: Four repos, two gates
body: VELA has 4 frontend repositories: three for the three portals, and a fourth that tracks VELA's data with the external systems it integrates with.
To be released, code had to pass Jasmine unit tests and a SonarQube quality gate.

beats.title: From Docker to Kubernetes
body: I implemented CI/CD pipelines that packaged the frontends as Docker images and deployed them to Kubernetes, across all 4 repositories.
I also refactored legacy UI modules, optimizing change detection at component level and moving them from Bootstrap to Tailwind, while production releases stayed stable.

sogus.title: SOGUS, two applications
sogus.role: Senior Frontend Developer, coordinating the frontend workstream. Project team of 10.
sogus.body: SOGUS screens candidates through online assessments, including multiple-choice and essay questions. It runs as two separate applications. Candidates get React/Next.js (Pages Router) for the landing, interview and testing flows, with SSR for SEO-critical pages and a fast first render. Internal administrators get an Angular portal. I designed the frontend architecture across both and coordinated the frontend workstream: task planning, progress tracking, PR review and coding standards.
sogus.tech: React, Next.js (SSR), TypeScript, Angular, Java, PostgreSQL
sogus.plateLabel: Illustrative drawing of SOGUS: a red block for candidates on React/Next.js and a blue block for internal administration on Angular, on one base plate.

medbuy.title: Medbuy, three sides
medbuy.role: Senior Frontend Developer. Project team of 10.
medbuy.body: Medbuy is an e-commerce platform connecting pharmaceutical suppliers, agents and end users. I built responsive, design-accurate interfaces in React/Next.js, working closely with UX/UI designers and using SSR for product and listing pages. I worked out REST API contracts with the backend team, integrated those APIs into the Next.js frontend, and took part in containerized deployment with Docker.
medbuy.plateLabel: Illustrative drawing of Medbuy: a red three-sided prism for suppliers, agents and end users, all outside the company.

kensa.title: Kensa, a team of two
kensa.role: Frontend Developer, fullstack on this project. Team of 2.
kensa.body: Kensa is an order management system with Admin and Customer portals: order tracking, revenue reporting, and self-service ordering and payment. I designed and built the system end to end: React on the front, Laravel REST APIs for order processing and reporting, MySQL underneath, and VNPay and Payoo for payment. I also deployed it and ran it in production on Linux with Docker.
kensa.plateLabel: Illustrative drawing of Kensa: a blue block for Admin and a red block for Customer, on one base plate with VNPay and Payoo attached.

items.body: I started at AMIT Group as a frontend intern, from June to December 2017. After graduating, I came back full-time in June 2018.
As a Frontend Developer, I built responsive web applications with React, Angular and WordPress for enterprise clients, and fullstack features with PHP/Laravel and MySQL.

As a Senior Frontend Developer, I built React/Next.js applications in TypeScript, wrote REST APIs with NestJS and Laravel, and led small frontend teams of 3–5: task planning, code review, technical mentoring. I deployed and maintained production applications on Linux, and worked directly with customers on estimates and scope.
